one_line_contribution: A consumer-side, one-forward-pass statistic — the consuming backbone's teacher-forced log-likelihood of a builder's stored action sequences — is proposed as the predictor of whether a shared experience bank helps that consumer, dominating builder capability/size/family, producing pre-registered cells where a weaker-but-closer builder's bank beats a stronger-but-distant one, and validated causally by a content-preserving re-narration that raises proximity with actions held fixed.
closest_prior_work: Verified: arXiv:2605.30723, 'Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment for LLM Agents' (2026-05-29, s2cli/S2+HF; full abstract truncated in S2 but the HF TLDR confirms 'model-aware skill alignment... hierarchical evolution and lightweight rewriter training'). It already establishes that identical skill text performs differently across backbones and already ships a trained rewriter that adapts skill wording per backbone — which is the proposal's re-narration arm in fitted form. It does not, from what I could verify, offer a cheap consumer-side offline predictor, run a full builder-by-consumer grid with the retrieved set held fixed, or claim a strength-versus-proximity dissociation, so it constrains rather than kills novelty; the proposal is right to treat it as 'repair, not predict.' Also verified and threatening: arXiv:2606.23127 (Managing Procedural Memory, 2026-06-22) already reports that some procedural skills generalize across model backbones and others lose effectiveness under transfer — the phenomenon exists in print; only the predictor is new. arXiv:2608.16647 ('Every Coin Has Two Sides: On the Dual Nature of Generalization in On-Policy Distillation', 2026-08-17, found via s2cli) states that distillation generalization is 'strongly tied to teacher-student origin alignment' — the same mechanism claim, in weight space rather than in context. The deepest threat is one the proposal never cites: the capacity-gap line in classical KD (arXiv:1902.03393 Teacher Assistant; arXiv:2311.07052 'Towards the Law of Capacity Gap'; arXiv:2605.23857 'Strong Teacher Not Needed?'), where 'a stronger teacher is not a better teacher for a distant student' is a settled result, and the likelihood-based demonstration-selection line (arXiv:2112.08633 EPR, which scores candidate in-context items by the consuming LM's own likelihood). Together these make 'closer beats stronger' and 'score the item under the consumer' familiar ideas that the proposal ports to in-context agent memory rather than invents; a reviewer who knows both literatures will discount the framing sharply. All IDs above were verified via the s2cli channel (S2 + HF Papers) except 1902.03393, 2311.07052, 2112.08633 and 2605.23857, which appeared as search hits in that same channel with titles and dates but which I did not individually re-verify with `s2cli paper`.
strongest_objection: Falsifiable Prediction (1) — the headline test — is rigged by degrees of freedom, not by mechanism. Policy proximity varies per (builder, consumer) cell: 64 distinct values. Its named competitors do not: builder solo success takes 8 values (one per builder), log parameter ratio is a coarse function of the same 8, and same-family is a binary. Against paired gains that vary cell-by-cell, essentially ANY cell-level statistic will beat a builder-level constant by more than 0.15 R-squared, including trivial ones — token overlap between the builder item and the consumer's own trajectories, plain unconditional perplexity of the item text under the consumer, or a tokenizer-vocabulary overlap score. Leave-one-builder-out CV does not repair this: it holds out builder-side variance while proximity keeps its consumer-side and item-side resolution. So the plan can satisfy Prediction (1) while the mechanism claim ('the consumer could plausibly have produced this action sequence') is false, and a reviewer will say the central result was decided by the predictor's granularity before a single episode ran. A second, compounding version of the same problem: proximity of a *successful* trajectory under the consumer is partly a measure of the consumer's own competence on that task type, and consumer competence is never entered as a competing predictor — so cells with high proximity may simply be cells where the consumer was already able, which the paired-gain outcome only partly cancels (headroom differs across consumers). The re-narration arm, which is supposed to carry the causal weight, has its own confound: consumer paraphrasing is an extra consumer forward pass over the memory, so any gain may be self-reflection/test-time compute over the item rather than raised proximity, and 'self-generated text is easier to follow' is an older ICL result (arXiv:2206.08082) that the design does not separate out.
what_would_fix_it: Three concrete changes, in order of importance. (1) Compare proximity only against predictors at matched granularity. Add at least three cell-level rivals that are cheaper or more trivial than proximity: unconditional perplexity of the retrieved item text under the consumer (no action conditioning, no teacher forcing); lexical/embedding overlap between the builder's stored trajectory and the consumer's own successful trajectories on the same task type; and tokenizer/format overlap. Re-state Prediction (1) as 'proximity beats the best cell-level rival by >=0.10 LOBO R-squared', and keep builder solo success only as a floor. If action-conditioned teacher-forced likelihood does not beat unconditional item perplexity, the specific mechanism claim dies and the paper still has an honest result — that is what a dissociation design should look like. (2) Enter consumer solo success and per-consumer headroom as covariates in the mixed-effects model and report proximity's within-consumer partial effect separately from the between-consumer effect; the reversal pairs are already within-consumer, so make them, not the R-squared, the headline. (3) Add a third-party paraphrase arm to the re-narration test: a fixed neutral model paraphrases the same items with actions held identical, giving a condition with the paraphrase operation but without the consumer's own wording. If consumer re-narration and neutral re-narration recover the same share of the gap, the recovery is a paraphrase/compute effect, not a proximity effect. Also cite and position against the KD capacity-gap literature and likelihood-based demonstration selection explicitly — the Related Work is entirely 2026 agent-memory papers and reads as if the older result does not exist.
missing_baseline: Two, and both are load-bearing. First, a granularity-matched cheap predictor — unconditional perplexity of the retrieved item under the consumer (and a lexical/embedding overlap score between builder items and the consumer's own trajectories). Without it, proximity's claimed advantage is only over builder-level constants and demonstrates nothing about the proposed mechanism. Second, consumer solo success as a competing predictor: the predictor list contains builder solo success, size ratio and family, but nothing about the consumer's own ability, even though the entire claim is that compatibility is a consumer-side property. A reviewer will ask whether 'proximity' is just 'this consumer is competent here' wearing a log-likelihood costume. Third, smaller: a third-model paraphrase control in the re-narration arm to separate 'consumer's own wording' from 'was paraphrased at all'.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is unusually good — it names channels, date windows, query strings, hit counts and specific IDs, admits that WebSearch was budget-exhausted and that the nearest paper's abstract was truncated, and does not treat empty returns as proof of novelty. That is above the norm for this pipeline and I credit it. My own searches, all answered by channel (a) the s2cli command (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers); channel (b) WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used for any query: (i) 'consumer model likelihood predicts whether shared agent experience memory transfers across backbones' --recent -> 10 hits, nearest 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap, already cited by the proposal), 2604.27003; nothing on a likelihood predictor. (ii) 'cross-model skill transfer compatibility teacher trajectory log-likelihood student policy similarity predictor' -> 12 hits, nearest 2608.16647 'Every Coin Has Two Sides' (2026-08-17), which ties on-policy distillation generalization to teacher-student origin alignment — the same mechanism intuition in weight space, not in-context memory; also 2605.12913. (iii) 'weaker teacher better than stronger teacher distillation student proximity capability gap' -> 2605.23857 'Strong Teacher Not Needed? On Distillation in LLM Pretraining' (2026-05-22), 2311.07052 'Law of Capacity Gap', 1902.03393 Teacher Assistant — the 'closer beats stronger' phenomenon is long published in weight-space KD, which the proposal's Related Work never acknowledges. (iv) named-method query on 2605.30723 -> retrieved it plus 2606.01139 'SkillRevise' (2026-06-02), which explicitly claims improved 'cross-model transferability' of revised skills and is not cited by the proposal — a near neighbour on the re-narration arm worth checking. (v) 'experience bank built by one LLM agent reused by another backbone builder consumer grid negative transfer' --recent -> 9 hits, nothing making the claim. (vi) 'perplexity of demonstration predicts in-context learning performance' -> 2112.08633 (EPR, LM-likelihood-based prompt retrieval), 2605.26350 'When Correct Demonstrations Hurt' — the likelihood-scoring family is old. (vii) 'model learns better from self-generated demonstrations / paraphrasing into own wording' -> 2206.08082 self-generated ICL. ID verification via `s2cli paper`: 2608.07169, 2605.30723, 2607.28048, 2604.04804, 2606.23127 and 2608.14036 all VERIFIED with matching titles and dates; 2607.10608 verified as a search hit. I did NOT verify 2604.03088 (SkVM), 2511.20639 (LatentMAS), 2605.30785, 2605.11032, 2608.03874, 2606.29961 or 2506.14728. Net judgement: the check is thorough inside the agent-memory neighbourhood and blind outside it — it ran no query on knowledge-distillation capacity gap or on likelihood-based demonstration selection, which is exactly where the strongest novelty threat lives, so its conclusion that 'nothing proposes a consumer-side likelihood predictor' is under-tested rather than established.
